title: Lloyd Price's big band and how Basie found him
summary: Wexler and Atlantic aside; Lloyd Price big band inspired Ray; Basie heard him in Wildwood and hired him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Sure. Yeah, I think a lot of people think they go in the record business and you make a lot of money. Oh, well on your Atlantic side, with Ray Charles, do you remember he had a producer, a guy named Jerry Wexler, did you remember Jerry? Yeah.
Okay. Did, what was- No, no, that name sounds familiar, I'm trying to picture who he is.

He was the A&R guy for Atlantic at that time. He was the other, one of their- Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. And he was one, he was one, fairly instrumental in aiding his career at Atlantic at the time. I just, I threw his name out to see if you-
Lloyd Price, didn't Lloyd Price record for Atlantic too? No, no.
No, he recorded for a specialty. Yes, that's a specialty. That's it. Did you work with Lloyd? Oh yeah, a lot of times.
I worked with his small band and then I worked with his big band when he had his big band. Like that record he had, You Are My Sunshine, and I was on that album. Oh yeah, that was with Ray.
Oh, that's right. Now Lloyd, Lloyd had a good big band. He had a much better band than Ray. Another thing that made Ray get a big band, cause the Lloyd band was so great.
Was that later in Lloyd's career? The big band?

No, he got that big band together about, when he got out of the service, about 50. Okay. Mid 50s? Yeah. Okay. And he got this band together. And Lloyd had a good big band. Ray had a small band. So I was playing with Lloyd at the time, and it was a big band in Atlanta, Georgia. And Ray played a concert there. We were playing at a club. So after Ray's concert, they came over to hear Lloyd's band. They had so much talk with Lloyd, they had a good band. And Ray told his manager, look, tomorrow we're going to get together and we're going to start getting musicians, and I'm going to get a big band too. And he liked the way Lloyd's band sounds. And the first time Count Basie approached me to sing, to play with his band, was because he heard Lloyd's band in Atlantic City. Now, Wildwood, New Jersey. So he wanted to know who was that trumpet player, playing lead trumpet. So he sent for me. Basie did. And I told him, you know, I was satisfied with where I was. Because I didn't know Basie, Basie had been out there a long time. I thought he had died out, because everything was rock and roll. And I thought that I would do better staying with Lloyd. I don't know, yeah, with Lloyd. So when he offered me a certain amount of money, I didn't know they were paying that kind of money. And I thought, oh yeah, man, so I went with Basie.
